cases.script:
# OR-007: Ester-limited hydrolysis leaves excess base
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 20mL
add v1 ethyl_acetate 0.005mol
add v1 NaOH 0.01mol
react v1 saponification
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
inspect
cases.original_forecast: A sufficiently large hydroxide budget can exhaust the ester while leaving an alkaline product solution.

original_criteria.criterion: The ester inventory approaches its modelled completion limit with appropriate acetate and ethanol formation.
The remaining base budget differs from the base-limited case; inspect acid/base speciation rather than looking for a NaOH molecule count alone.

original_limitations: The react command requests a named teaching transformation; it does not demonstrate spontaneous room-temperature chemistry, a real mechanism, or a reaction rate.

The aqueous solver may distribute acid/base inventory among ions and neutral forms before react. Check named-transformation ownership explicitly; no successful execution has been inferred from the reaction table alone.

cases.script:
# OR-008: Acidifying a saponification product does not automatically remake ester
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 20mL
add v1 ethyl_acetate 0.001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
react v1 saponification
inspect v1
add v1 HCl 0.001mol
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
inspect
cases.original_forecast: Acidification shifts acetate toward acetic acid. Without a new esterification request, that protonation is not itself evidence of ester re-formation.

original_criteria.criterion: The acetic-acid fraction increases after acid addition.
Separate proton-transfer changes from any actual C–O bond-forming esterification; no automatic reversed saponification is assumed.

original_limitations: The react command requests a named teaching transformation; it does not demonstrate spontaneous room-temperature chemistry, a real mechanism, or a reaction rate.

cases.script:
# OR-009: Follow carbon through esterification and alkaline cleavage
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 CH3COOH 0.01mol
add v1 ethanol 0.01mol
react v1 esterification
inspect v1
add v1 water 20mL
add v1 NaOH 0.02mol
react v1 saponification
inspect v1
cases.original_forecast: Ester made in the first transformation is cleaved in the second; initially unreacted acid also consumes part of the hydroxide budget.

original_criteria.criterion: Compute carbon across acid/acetate, ethanol and ester before and after both transformations.
Do not assign all added base to ester cleavage: neutralisation of residual acetic acid is a separate demand.

original_limitations: The react command requests a named teaching transformation; it does not demonstrate spontaneous room-temperature chemistry, a real mechanism, or a reaction rate.
